candidate_tasks.primary_question: Does a turnover-matched coin-flip null change the cost-robustness verdict for the momentum candidate relative to the standard coin-flip null?
candidate_tasks.bottleneck: The standard coin-flip null trades far more than the low-turnover momentum signal, so under costs its dispersion changes and the matched-null comparison is asymmetric; n_edge can shift without any candidate-median change.
candidate_tasks.objective: Implement and run a turnover-matched null (coin-flip signals with the same per-bar turnover as the momentum signal) under the realistic cost model and compare the cost-robustness classification to the standard null.
candidate_tasks.scope: Use the existing 10-asset universe, the existing momentum signal, and a turnover-matched null variant; bounded comparison only.
candidate_tasks.out_of_scope: Do not tune the signal, expand the universe, or change the cost model.
candidate_tasks.deliverable: A reproducible artifact and independent verification comparing turnover-matched vs standard null cost-robustness verdicts.
candidate_tasks.success_criterion: The comparison yields a clear classification (verdict unchanged or changed) with the exact figures.
candidate_tasks.stop_condition: Stop after the turnover-matched null is evaluated and independently checked.
candidate_tasks.verification_requirement: Leakage, matched null, independent recomputation, determinism, regression suite.
candidate_tasks.evidence_basis: R-001 found the standard coin-flip null trades more than the low-turnover signal, making n_edge null-dispersion-sensitive under costs.
